summary: In Hidalgo County, Billy watches wolves chase antelope, and later he and Boyd meet an Indian.
Billy, Boyd and their father ride to the SK Bar and search Echols' cabin for traps.
Billy and his father wax the traps and ride into the Peloncillos to make their first sets.
The she-wolf comes north from Sonora into the Peloncillos, and Billy and his father work their trapline.
Billy places traps toward Hog Canyon and talks with an elderly rancher driving a Model A.
Billy's father tries a new way of burying traps, and Billy returns to Echols' cabin for scents.
Billy rides to Animas to seek advice about the wolf from old Don Arnulfo.
Billy finds a track at the vaqueros' campfire near Cloverdale and buries a trap in the ashes.
Billy rides south across the border into Sonora and up the Cajón Bonito trail.
Billy follows riders to a hacienda beside the Batopito River.
Billy rides through the mountains of Mexico and hears a tale from a hermit in a ruined church.
Billy takes leave of his host in the empty town and sets out for home.
Billy rides north along the river through Bacerac and Bavispe toward the border crossing at Douglas.
Billy rides the old road over the Guadalupes and across the Animas Plain toward home.
Billy returns to the family house, then rides through Animas toward Lordsburg.
Billy sits across the desk from the Lordsburg sheriff and answers his questions.
Billy and Boyd ride together from Lordsburg through Arizona and south into Mexico.
Billy and Boyd ride from Bacerac over the mountains toward Casas Grandes.
Billy, Boyd and a girl arrive at the Hacienda de San Diego, where traveling opera singers are staying.
The brothers and the girl camp beside the river, and Billy fixes a nail in Boyd's boot.
Camping where an old wagon road runs toward Namiquipa, Billy talks with an old man driving oxen.
The brothers ride south through rain in the pine mountains to the railroad town of Las Varas.
At a windmill tank on the high prairie, the brothers water the horses and talk.
At noon the brothers ride into Boquilla y Anexas, and Billy buys rope at the store.
In Boquilla y Anexas the brothers eat street tacos and nap under trees in the town square.
The brothers head west to the river, then ride north toward the small village of San José.
Near midnight Billy reaches a remote house where a blind man and his wife tell a long story.
In Casas Grandes before dawn, a servant opens the gate of a walled house to Billy.
At San Diego the brothers talk, and a servant from town rides in on a burro leading Niño.
Billy rides south from San Diego, through Mata Ortiz and Boquilla, toward Namiquipa.
Billy spends his days at San Diego helping herders bring sheep in for shearing.
Billy saddles his horse at San Diego and rides south along the road in gray weather.
Billy crosses back into New Mexico at Columbus and tries to enlist in the army.
Billy camps on the Animas Plain, then drifts from ranch job to ranch job through the war years.
Billy enters Chihuahua at Berendo and rides to Janos, where he stops at a cantina.
Billy shelters in Janos for the night, then rides south through country he crossed with Boyd.
Billy comes to Namiquipa asking questions, then rides through the Babícora country.
Billy rides north through the rain to the town of San Buenaventura.
Billy keeps camp by the river and shares supper with a talkative American rider.
Billy rides north along the river and crosses the border into New Mexico.
Billy wakes in his roadside shelter and walks out onto the desert road.
